column2: One who foretells ill for the king, one who abuses him, one who sells what clings to a dead body, one who strikes a teacher,
and one who betrays his counsel — having cut the tongue one should banish him. One who mounts the king's vehicle or seat gets the middle fine of violence;
one who pierces both eyes, or follows an order of the king's enemy, and a Shudra living as a Brahmin — a fine of eight hundred.
One who thinks "I am not defeated," though defeated by law — having defeated him again as he comes, one should punish him with a double fine.
The fine taken by the king by law, dedicated to Varuna, should be announced and given to Brahmins, himself increasing it thirtyfold.
Dharma, wealth, fame, the company of the people, support, great honor from the subjects and an eternal heavenly station —
for the king who sees legal cases there would be these seven qualities.
One becomes unassailable by all beings, without doubt. One should salute the sun at the three twilights with "Chitram";
a man with fuel in hand always obtains the wealth desired. Then reciting "Atha svapna" in the morning and midday,
he destroys a bad dream entirely and obtains good food. "Ubhe pumanti" likewise is declared the demon-slayer;
reciting the verses "Ubhe vasa" one obtains desires; reciting "Na sagan" one is freed from aggressors;
reciting "Kaya shubha" one obtains eminence of birth; "Imam nri somam" — one obtains all desires;
with "Pitar" one should attend; wealth comes ever near. With the hymn "Agne naya" and a ghee oblation, a traveler on the road
obtains a hero's good conduct; one who always recites the good verse; with the hymn "Kankato na" one removes all poisons;
with the hymn "Yo jata" one obtains all desires; with the hymn "Ganananam" one obtains the best affection;
Yo me rajan is the verse that quiets bad dreams. One who, setting out on a road, sees an enemy risen,
inauspicious or auspicious, should recite "Kuvid anga imam." Reciting the twenty-second hymn, the supreme spiritual one,
on festivals, pure, one always obtains desired wishes. Reciting the hymn "Krinushva," offering ghee with concentration,
one may take the lives of enemies and also destroy demons. One should attend the fire himself day by day with the verse "Pari";
that fire itself protects him, the all-faced from all sides. "Hamsah shuchishat" — the pure should look at the sun.
One who undertakes farming should offer the sthalipaka by rule in the middle of the field with five "svaha" offerings:
to Indra, the Maruts, Parjanya, Bhaga; the farmer should till with the plough as marked;
for grain, to Sita (the furrow), Sunasira next; with scents, garlands and salutations one should worship these deities.
In sowing, reaping, threshing and carrying home the furrow-crop, the work is unfailing and farming ever prospers.
With the hymn "Samudrat" one obtains desires from fire; one who, with two verses "Vaishvanara," is worthy of fire
crosses all calamities and obtains imperishable fame; obtains abundant prosperity and the highest victory.
Having praised with "Agne tvam" one obtains the desired wealth. One desiring offspring should recite always the three for Varuna;
one should recite the three of "Svasti" in the morning, always a great blessing; having uttered "Svasti pantha" one goes safely on the road.
Vanaspate for the conqueror: illness for enemies. For a woman bewildered in pregnancy, the best release of the child.
One desiring rain should apply the hymn "Achchhavada"; fasting, with wet clothes, it rains before long.
A man desiring cattle should recite "Manasah kama"; one desiring offspring, pure in vow, should bathe with "Kardamena";
a man desiring kingdom should bathe with "Ashvapurva"; a Brahmin should bathe on a red hide by rule;
a king on a tiger hide, and a Vaishya likewise on a goat hide; ten thousand oblations are declared for each.
With the hymn "Agara" one should approach and go to the cow, mother of the world, in the cow-pen, if one wishes them ever imperishable.
With "Upa" and three, one should consecrate the king's drum; one obtains splendor and strength and restrains the enemy.
Holding grass in hand, surrounded by bandits, one should recite the demon-slaying hymn; reciting "Ye ke cha uma" one obtains long life.
With the Jimuta hymn one should consecrate the army's limbs; then the king, as marked, kills enemies in battle.
With three Agneya hymns one obtains imperishable wealth; with the hymn "Amivaha" one should settle beings at night.
In an obstructed, uneven fort, or bound, or having escaped anywhere, fleeing or seized, one should recite this hymn too.
Having fasted three nights restrained, one should cook a pudding offering; with it a full hundred oblations one should make with the verse "Tryambaka."
Addressing Mahadeva, one lives a hundred years happily. Bathed, with the verse "Tach chakshuh" one should attend the sun,
rising and in the middle of the sky, wishing long life. The hymn "Indra-Soma" is said to destroy enemies.
One whose vow has lapsed through delusion or who associates with outcastes should fast and offer ghee: "Tvam agne vratapa."
Having recited the verse "Aditya" and "Samrajam," one becomes victorious in debate; with the four-verse "Mahi" one is freed from great fear.
Having recited the "Mahi" verse, one would obtain all desires. Reciting the forty-two Indra verses one destroys enemies;
reciting "Vacham mahi" one obtains health too. With two verses "Shanno bhava," having eaten food pure and restrained,
touching the heart with the hand, one is not overcome by diseases. "Uttamedam," having bathed and offered, one may kill an enemy.
With the hymn "Shanno agni," by the oblation one obtains food; with the Kanya-varshi hymn one is freed from directional faults.
When "Yad atya kavye" is uttered and recited, the world surely prospers; by reciting "Yad vag," speech becomes refined.
Reciting "Vacho viditam" one gains speech. The "Pavamani" verses are held as the purifier of purifiers.
The thirty Vaikhanasa verses are held supreme purifiers; sixty-two verses are said, "Parasva," best of sages,
for destruction of all sin, for purification and for auspiciousness. Sixty-seven are declared of the "Svadishtha" hymns;
these Pavamani verses are six hundred and ten. Reciting and offering this one conquers the terrible fear of death.
One standing in water should recite "Apo hishtha" for removal of fear of sin; and in a desert, restrained, "Pra devanna";
when fear at the end of life arrives, one quickly gains life. One should mentally recite the single verse "Praveyam" at night;
at dawn, with sunrise, one obtains victory in gambling. By "Ma pragama" the bewildered finds the path on the road.
Whoever one considers of failing life, any dear friend: bathed, with "Yat teyam," one should touch his head
a thousand times for five days; by that he gains great life. The wise should offer ghee a thousand times with "Idam medhya";
one desiring cattle in a cow-pen, one desiring wealth at a crossroads, reciting "Vayah suparna" gains prosperity.
Having repeated "Havishyanti" one is freed from all sins; his diseases perish and the body's fire increases.
Ya oshadhayah is a blessing, destroyer of all diseases; "Brihaspate ati" one desiring rain should use;
Sarvatra is to be known as supreme peace, and "Pratiratha"; "Suta Sankashyapa" is declared for one desiring offspring.
Aham rudra — thereby a man becomes eloquent; the learned one reciting "Ratri" at night is not born from a womb.
A man reciting the Night hymn at night conquers the night safely; reciting "Kalpayanti" always he makes destruction of enemies.
The great hymn of Dakshayana gives long life and splendor; one steady in vow should recite "Uta deva" as the destroyer of illness.
When there is fear of fire one should recite "Ayam agne jani"; in forests one should recite "Aranyani," destroying that fear.
Having obtained brahmi and shatavari with the two hymns and the verse "Brahmi," separately with water or ghee one gains intelligence and prosperity.
Masa is the destroyer of rivals for one desiring victory in battle; "Brahmano agnih sam vidanah" prevents miscarriage death;
one should recite the hymn "Apa hi," pure, destroying bad dreams; having recited "Yenedam," one gains supreme concentration.
Mayo bhur vata is the supreme blessing for cows; by it one wards off Shambari, Indra's net or illusion.
Mahi trinam avarastu one should recite as a blessing on the road; "Agnaye vidvishan" thus one should recite for destruction of enemies.
One should worship the house deities with the mantra "Vastoshpate"; this rule is stated for recitation, and for oblation it is to be known specially.
At the end of the oblation a fee should be given; pacification of sin by the offering; the offering is calmed by food, by giving food and gold;
the blessings of Brahmins would be unfailing; an outer bath everywhere; mustard seeds, barley, grain, milk and ghee,
milk-tree fuel too — these oblations give all desires. Fuel sticks, thorny plants, mustard, blood and poison (for hostile rites).
